clue.text: Assistant editor given pamphlet to take away

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, is an assistant editor on a newspaper
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A junior newspaper editor is handed a leaflet to carry off.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct a number is to remove it from another in arithmetic.

clue.text: Fellow initially indisposed to supply grass-cutters

indicators.note: initially says the word for unwell comes first, ahead of the man's name

parts.note: indisposed means unwell or sick
Les is a man's name, so any fellow

explanation.surface: A man first feeling unwell nonetheless provides tools for mowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it is the charade's placing word; 'Fellow' is a man's first name, a common crossword convention, and 'to supply' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved hand blades were used for reaping crops and cutting long grass.

clue.text: Jollification for the enjoyment of runners, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a lively celebration or party with food

definitions.text: for the enjoyment of runners, perhaps
definitions.meaning: runner beans read whimsically as guests at a meal laid on for them

explanation.surface: A party laid on to entertain athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests athletes, but it means runner beans, a common British garden vegetable; the question-mark 'perhaps' flags them as an example of beans.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British word for a jolly celebration or works outing with a big meal.

clue.text: Secured again, run in, and taken back to court

indicators.note: in means the run letter goes inside the word for fastened once more

parts.note: to secure something again with a knot is to have retied it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A prisoner, recaptured, brought in and hauled before the judge again.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard a second time by a court has been put on trial again.

clue.text: Polished ring thrown in abruptly

indicators.note: thrown in means the ring shape is inserted into the word for brusquely

parts.note: to speak curtly is to speak abruptly
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A refined ring is tossed in hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished manners of a refined and elegant kind are what a royal court was known for.

clue.text: Son of corpulent build, short and thick

parts.note: tubby means fat or corpulent

explanation.surface: A description of a stocky boy whose build is portly, squat and thickset.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers or legs described as squat and fat are said to be thickset in exactly this way.

clue.text: Incidental information is brought up with great pleasure

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: delight is great pleasure

explanation.surface: A minor fact is raised with much enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A side remark that casts some light on a subject is extra, incidental detail.

clue.text: Experience governed by vitality

parts.note: under means subject to or governed by, as under a ruler
go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: Someone experienced is ruled by their energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through or suffer something, such as surgery, is to experience it.

clue.text: Left-wing nonsense that's written about Lenin's origin

indicators.note: about means the word for rubbish is placed around the Lenin letter

parts.note: bosh is a dated word for nonsense

indicators.note: origin points to the initial letter of Lenin

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A dismissal of the rubbish written about the Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' is only a link word. The surface hints at a Bolshevik text, which suits the word's origin as a short form of that party name.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word, from Bolshevik, for someone rebellious or with left-wing views.

clue.text: He tries to stop gentlemen running on the beach

definitions.text: He tries to stop gentlemen running on the beach

parts.words: He tries to stop gentlemen running on the beach
parts.note: the gentlemen are smugglers, as in Kipling's poem, and running means smuggling goods ashore; the man patrolling the shore tries to stop them

explanation.surface: Someone tries to halt well-dressed men jogging along the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentlemen' was an old euphemism for smugglers, and to 'run' contraband is to smuggle it ashore, so this is no fitness scene but a shore patrol at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore patrol officer's historic job was intercepting smugglers landing contraband on the coast.

clue.text: Troll finally escorted back, to wooded hollow

indicators.note: back tells us the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction
finally points to the closing letter of the word Troll

parts.note: to escort someone is to lead them, past tense led

explanation.surface: A troll is finally walked back home to a hollow in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives L from Troll; add LED and 'back' turns LLED round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A small valley among trees is the classic picture of this word, as in 'the farmer in the...'.

clue.text: Deserted radicals defeated in a game

parts.note: the Left is the collective name for radical or socialist politicians
a lurch is a heavy defeat in cribbage and some other games, so a player beaten that way is caught in one

explanation.surface: Abandoned extremists lost a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lurch' was originally a crushing defeat in an old board game and survives in cribbage scoring; the phrase came to mean abandoned in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abandoned by companions at a difficult moment is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Be prepared to act for champion?

definitions.meaning: to be ready to go into action at short notice, as a reserve or emergency service
to champion someone is to support or stick loyally with them

explanation.surface: A substitute is told to get ready to take the place of the title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'champion' is a verb here (support), not a title holder, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on alert as a reserve and loyally supporting someone are both common senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Supporter sheltering Tyler in a remote place

indicators.note: sheltering means the supporter word protects and surrounds the rebel's name

parts.note: a backer is a financial or moral supporter
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A backer hides an outlaw in a far-off spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagnant stretch of river off the main stream gives its name to an isolated, sleepy spot.

clue.text: Disregarded point I blush about

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the phrase for blushing surrounds the compass point

parts.note: to blush is to go red
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone who has been snubbed admits to reddening over a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blush' is the two-word phrase GO RED, and 'about' puts N inside it: G(N)ORED, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked or paid no attention to has been deliberately passed over.

clue.text: Agent with farming land apt for restoration

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
arable land is land used for growing crops

explanation.surface: A land agent handles fields suitable for renovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being mended or fixed is repairable.

clue.text: Screen the French put round an upper room

indicators.note: put round means the French article wraps around the room word

parts.note: le is French for the
an attic is a room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A screen is placed around a French loft room.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of crossed strips forms a see-through partition or window screen.

clue.text: Severe wind from south and east

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

explanation.surface: A harsh gale blowing from the south and east.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern, strict and plain, a severe manner or style is spartan.

clue.text: Vessel built with Asian capital, mostly, inside Thailand's borders

indicators.note: inside means the shortened capital sits within the outer letters of Thailand
borders means only the first and last letters of Thailand are used
mostly means the capital loses its last letter

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, which lies largely in Asia

explanation.surface: A ship built with funds from an Asian city, mostly within Thai frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a drinking mug. 'mostly' cuts ANKARA to ANKAR; 'borders' gives T and D from Thailand's.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beer mug, often pewter with a handle, is a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Like mail with labels put on flight out East

definitions.text: Like mail with labels put on

indicators.note: out tells us a letter is dropped from the word for flight

parts.note: a stampede is a sudden panicked flight of animals or people

explanation.surface: Letters with stickers attached are sent on a plane heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air mail, but it is a panicked rush; 'out' removes one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Post bearing postage labels has been franked or marked for sending.

clue.text: Student of the sun receiving high honour

indicators.note: receiving means the word for sun-related takes the honour letters inside it

parts.note: solar means of the sun
CH, Companion of Honour, is a high British honour

explanation.surface: An astronomy student is given a top award.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person or pupil who studies is a learner or academic.

clue.text: A gap one can make at the highest point

indicators.note: can make says these letters can be formed into another word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A space one can create at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped a letter of 'point'; the printed page has it. The word describes an orbit's furthest point from Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Relates to the apogee, the point of an orbit farthest from Earth, hence the climax or peak.

clue.text: Assistant in theatre who takes care of wounds?

definitions.meaning: a backstage helper who looks after an actor's costumes and helps them change
someone who applies bandages to injuries

explanation.surface: A backstage helper who also patches up injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests an operating theatre, which suits the wounds, but the first sense is the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a costume helper backstage and someone who bandages injuries carry this job title.

clue.text: Scholars may take this part of meal after port

indicators.note: after says the meal part follows the port in the answer

parts.note: Sandwich is an old port town in Kent, England
a course is one stage of a meal, such as the soup or dessert

explanation.surface: Students might eat this dish once the port has been passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the after-dinner drink, but it is Sandwich, a historic port town in Kent, England. A course of this kind alternates college study with periods of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Students can follow a programme mixing college terms with work placements, which bears this name.

clue.text: In part she ranks as queen of the gods

indicators.note: In part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Partly, she is rated as the queen of the Olympians.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'as', which is only a link: 'as queen of the gods' cannot stand for a name, so the definition is 'queen of the gods'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus's wife ruled Olympus beside him as its queen.

clue.text: It travels freely by routes, without lines

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the lines
freely says the letters of by routes are moved about at will

parts.note: L is short for line, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A vehicle moves at will along its routes with no track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' makes TROEYBUS from 'by routes'; 'without' (outside) puts that round LL. The joke is that this vehicle needs overhead lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric bus drawing power from overhead wires is a passenger vehicle that carries people about.

clue.text: American conductor's songs for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: A US orchestra director's recital pieces for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage this word means an orchestra's conductor; in Britain it means the principal violinist. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English the person directing a band or orchestra is called by this title.

clue.text: King and Queen taking in university's magnificence

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is a royal cipher for King George

indicators.note: taking in means the queen's letters enclose the university letter

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for Queen Elizabeth
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A royal couple visiting a university show off its splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour and impressive grandeur of scale are what this noun names.
